text:
Anika: Heads-up: canary for northstar-int8-1 on funcall flows showing a spike in parse failures — outputs that should be JSON are frequently rejected by the parser.
Joseph: https://console.redwood/canary/northstar-int8-1 | parse_failure_rate = 2.6% (last 2h) vs 0.2% baseline :eyes:
Anika: Sample problematic output (copied from raw stream):
```json
{ "action": "open_file", "path": "/tmp/logs/2026-03-19.log" }
ok done
```
The trailing "ok done" appears to be the culprit for the parser — it's valid tokens but breaks strict toolcall parsing.
Matt: Could be kv-cache/batch boundary truncation or EOS token leakage. We saw similar token-boundary artifacts in other quantized canaries.
Anika: Correlates with short prompt + kvcache hitrate >70%. Also more common when sequence length < 80.
Eva: Can you paste the raw token stream snippet (escaped)?
Anika: ```
[106, 45, 123, 34, 97, 99, 116, 105, 111, 110, 34, 58, 32, 34, 111, 112, 101, 110, 95, 102, 105, 108, 101, 34, 44, 32, 34, 112, 97, 116, 104, 34, 58, 32, 34, 47, 116, 109, 112, 47, 108, 111, 103, 115, 47, 50, 48, 50, 54, 45, 48, 51, 45, 49, 57, 46, 108, 111, 103, 34, 125, 10, 111, 107, 32, 100, 111, 110, 101]
```
Sam: Quick plan: 1) disable kv-prefix caching on the canary for 1h; 2) enable a lightweight soft-json-repair fallback (strip trailing non-json after last brace, attempt to reparse). I can schedule a canary config change.
deploy-bot: Canary update scheduled: northstar-int8-1 {soft_json_repair=true, kvcache_prefix=false} (deployment id: cbd-5678)
Joseph: Also try tightening the stop tokens and add explicit end marker in the prompt. Quantized runs sometimes append a polite phrase after structured output.
Anika: Good call. I'll add stop sequence "
### END_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT" and bump parser retry budget to 3 with 200ms exponential backoff.
Matt: If we apply auto-repair we must label telemetry accordingly so we don't silently hide regressions. Add a tag/field repair_mode in parse events.
Anika: Logging patch incoming — parse telemetry will include "repair_mode": "none|soft_repair|hard_repair" and "repair_applied": true/false.
Eva: I'll run a 50q synthetic sweep with the canary changes (soft-repair + stops + kvcache off) and post results.
(2 hours later)
Anika: Patch results after ~2h: parse_failure_rate dropped from 2.6% -> 0.45%. repair_applied: 18% of calls. Bad repair rate (false positives where repaired JSON changed semantics): ~0.1%.
Sam: Promising. Next steps: roll to 10% for another 24h, run full regression eval against "funcall-schema-set-A" to ensure no semantic regressions, and add a gating alert if repaired_fraction > 25%.
Joseph: Also pin the quant config for the rollout and disable auto-promotion in the platform for this model until we pass evals.
Anika: Will do and will file follow-up ticket INF-3427 with the canary logs, config diffs, and eval artifacts.
Matt: Thanks — also add an integration test that injects trailing non-json tokens to the parser to ensure the repair heuristic doesn't overfit to this canary.
Anika: On it.
Sam: Nice collaborative quick loop :thumbsup:
